Additionally, several of the products and compounds discussed today are being developed in collaboration with strategic partners or licensed from other companies. This slide acknowledges those relationships. Moving to today's agenda, Joaquin Duato, our Chairman and CEO, will discuss our business performance and

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: growth drivers. I will then review the third-quarter sales and P&L results. Joe Wolk, our CFO, will then close by sharing an overview of our capital allocation priorities and updated guidance for 2026. Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine; John Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development; and Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech, will be joining us for Q&A. To ensure we provide enough time to address your questions, we anticipate the webcast will last approximately 60 minutes. With that, I will now turn the call over to Joaquin.

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO: Thank you, Ryan, and good morning, everyone. Our strong performance in the third quarter reinforces our confidence in 2026 as a year of accelerated growth and impact for Johnson & Johnson. In Q3, we reported operational sales growth of 6%, ahead of analyst consensus, and increased sequential growth compared to the second quarter. With six strategic focus areas—oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, surgery, and vision—we are leading in areas of higher medical need where innovation can make the greatest difference for patients. Our powerful combination of Innovative Medicine and MedTech expertise strengthens our competitiveness. Twenty-nine of our products and platforms now generate at least $1 billion in annual sales. Our marketed portfolio continues to perform. Our launches are gaining significant traction, and we are advancing our new product pipeline that will sustain our growth into the next decade. With sales in the quarter of more than $25 billion, we are on track to meet our guidance and exceed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time in our company's 140-year history. As we advance our differentiated portfolio and pipeline, we have a clear path to double-digit growth by the end of the decade. In Innovative Medicine, we delivered operational sales growth of 7.9%, with eight brands growing double digits. Let's start with oncology. We are making progress to redefine care from treatment to cure. In the third quarter,

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: our oncology business grew by approximately 17%. Our multiple myeloma portfolio and pipeline are unmatched, with 80% of patients receiving a Johnson & Johnson therapy as part of their treatment journey. We continue to strengthen the body of evidence supporting our recently launched multiple myeloma therapies and combination regimens. New Phase 3 results announced in July demonstrated that the combination of Gvalli plus Talvey reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 89%, as early as the second line of treatment. In solid tumors, sales of RYBREVANT increased by 64%, reflecting its strength in lung cancer. By the end of the year, we expect to receive U.S. FDA approval for RYBREVANT Faspro in advanced head and neck cancer, a disease with significant unmet needs. In bladder cancer, INLEXZO has rapidly emerged as a market leader for new patient share, just one year after its launch. Nearly one in three eligible patients started on an INLEXZO regimen in the third quarter, demonstrating its growing role in transforming care in high-risk non-muscle-invasive disease. During the quarter, we also invested to bolster our oncology pipeline. We completed our acquisition of Firefly Bio, adding a promising new degrader antibody-conjugate platform that targets drivers of difficult-to-treat cancers, including KRAS. Our ambition is to become the number one oncology company by 2030, with sales projected to exceed $50 billion. Turning to immunology, we are building on our 25-year

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: legacy to drive industry-leading innovation for patients. Tremfya delivered exceptional sales growth of 68% in the quarter, reflecting strong momentum across its indications. In the U.S., it is now the number one IL-23 inhibitor in new-to-brand share in Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and psoriatic arthritis. We continue to generate evidence that reinforces Tremfya's clinical differentiation. Based on the landmark STARS study, Tremfya is the first and only IL-23 inhibitor to demonstrate positive outcomes in axial disease clinical trials, including significant improvement in spinal pain, stiffness, and inflammation in patients with psoriatic arthritis. This momentum reinforces our conviction in Tremfya as a foundational medicine in inflammatory bowel and psoriatic diseases and our belief that it can grow into a $10 billion-plus franchise. ICOTYDE, our first-in-class targeted oral peptide for plaque psoriasis, continues to outpace recent competitor launches. More than 20,000 patients have initiated therapy through nearly 9,000 prescribers since ICOTYDE's launch in the U.S. We continue to make strong progress on commercial access, with ICOTYDE now broadly covered across all national plans. Also this quarter, IMDEE was approved as the first advanced treatment specifically for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a rare, life-threatening disease that causes severe anemia and fatigue. This new indication builds on IMDEE's momentum in generalized myasthenia gravis and reflects

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: its broad potential across autoantibody diseases. We continue to pursue next-generation therapies. In July, we announced a collaboration with Cell BioMedicines to advance in vivo CAR T approaches for immune-mediated diseases. Next, in neuroscience, we aim to transform the future of brain health by addressing complex nervous system disorders. Today, we are the definitive leader in neuropsychiatry. CAPLYTA reached $1 billion in year-to-date sales, making it our 29th billion-dollar platform. This was driven by strong uptake as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder. CAPLYTA is now the fastest-growing oral branded therapy in this space. Last month, we presented pivotal Phase 3 data that showed CAPLYTA significantly and rapidly improved symptoms of bipolar mania. SPRAVATO also delivered impressive growth of 36% this quarter, reflecting strong demand in treatment-resistant depression. Now let's turn to MedTech, where we delivered Q3 operational sales growth of 2.5%. While we fell short of our expectations for the segment, our conviction in our future direction has not changed. Starting with cardiovascular, we continue to invest in heart recovery, circulatory restoration, and heart rhythm disorders to address the leading global cause of death. This was another strong quarter for Shockwave, our circulatory restoration business, which grew 17%. The ongoing global launch of Shockwave C2 Aero continues to broaden the reach of our intravascular lithotripsy platforms.

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: VARIPULSE, our pulsed-field ablation platform, reached a major milestone this quarter, with more than 100,000 AFib patients treated worldwide. VARIPULSE Pro, which delivers five-times-faster ablation speed, has been very well received in Europe, where it is driving double-digit growth. Just last week, we received approval for VARIPULSE Pro in Japan. With increasing clinical experience, we are seeing differentiated benefits from VARIPULSE. In a recent retrospective analysis, VARIPULSE demonstrated a 68% lower risk of adverse cardiac events compared to a competing pulsed-field ablation platform. In heart recovery, while physician selection continued to affect Abiomed's performance, we remain confident in the technology and focused on supporting appropriate patient selection. In surgery, we are poised to shape the next era of care through robotics, digital innovation, and advanced instrumentation. In July, the U.S. FDA granted de novo authorization for OTTAVA, the world's first stable and integrated soft-tissue robotic system. This is one of the most significant MedTech innovations we will bring to market this decade. OTTAVA's unique architecture, automated features, and next-generation robotic instruments help address surgeon needs for operating-room space and better surgical workflows. Its connection to our open digital ecosystem, Polyphonic, turns procedure data into actionable insights for clinicians. We already signed our first commercial customer for OTTAVA, and we are

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: progressing our development program. Our investigational device exemption trial is already underway in inguinal hernia repair, with future plans for indication expansion into urology and gynecology. Finally, in vision, we are advancing lifelong eye health to bring better sight to more than 40 million people each year. The recent U.S. launch of TECNIS PureSee further strengthened our portfolio of intraocular lenses. During the quarter, TECNIS PureSee and TECNIS Odyssey surpassed one million implants worldwide, reflecting continued surgeon adoption and our leadership in personalized vision solutions. We also received CE marking for ACUVUE OASYS MAX two-week reusable lenses, expanding our ACUVUE portfolio in Europe. Overall, this quarter's strong results demonstrate the impact of the choices we have made to build a foundation for durable growth. We have sharpened our portfolio to focus on innovation with the greatest potential to change lives. We have proved our ability to grow through a significant loss of exclusivity. Our strategic investments in high-growth areas are delivering results, and our innovation engine continues to drive breakthroughs for patients. That is why we have the confidence to say that we will finish 2026 strong and that 2027 will be an even better year for Johnson & Johnson. I will now turn the call back over to Ryan.

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations: Thank you, Joaquin. Moving to our financial results. Unless otherwise stated, the percentages quoted represent operational results and therefore exclude the impact of currency translation. Starting with Q3 2026 sales results, worldwide sales were $25.4 billion for the quarter, increasing 6%. Growth in the U.S. was 9.1% and 1.8% outside the U.S. Acquisitions and divestitures had a net negative impact on worldwide growth of 10 basis points. Now turning to earnings. For the quarter, net earnings were $210 million and diluted earnings per share were $0.09 versus $2.12 a year ago. Results in the quarter were impacted by the proposed talc litigation resolution, as well as expenses associated with the Firefly Bio transaction and Cell BioMedicines collaboration, amounting to approximately $7 billion. Adjusted net earnings for the quarter were $6.3 billion, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $2.59, representing a decrease of 6.8% and 7.5%, respectively, compared to the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted earnings in the quarter were also impacted by expenses associated with the Firefly Bio transaction and Cell BioMedicines collaboration. I will now comment on business sales results in the quarter, focusing on the six key areas where meaningful innovation and strong commercial execution are driving our performance and fueling long-term growth. Beginning with Innovative Medicine, where our financial results reflect the depth of our

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: expertise and innovation in areas of high unmet need across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. Worldwide sales of $16.8 billion increased 7.9%, which underscores the continued strength of our key brands and new launches. Growth in the U.S. was 11.1% and 3% outside the U.S. Divestitures had a negative impact of 10 basis points on worldwide growth. In oncology, starting with multiple myeloma, DARZALEX growth was 15.6%, primarily driven by strong share gains of five points across all lines of therapy, with 10 points in the frontline setting, as well as continued market growth, partially offset by O-U.S. pricing headwinds. PRAVYCTI achieved growth of 35.2%, driven by share gains across earlier lines of therapy and continued site expansion. TECVAYLI growth was 77.3%, driven by launch uptake and share gains across earlier lines of therapy following last quarter's approval in the U.S. TALVEY plus DARZALEX FASPRO U.S. growth was over 100%. TALVEY growth was 42.1%, driven by share gains due to increased depth of prescribing in the community setting. In lung cancer, RYBREVANT plus lazertinib delivered growth of 63.5%, with strong share gains in the first and second lines driven by continued launch uptake in all regions, along with rapid uptake in RYBREVANT FASPRO. In prostate cancer, ERLEADA delivered growth of 9.4%, with continued share gains and market growth, partially offset by unfavorable patient mix. Within immunology, Tremfya delivered impressive growth of 68.2%, driven

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: by continued momentum from the IBD launch, with four points of share growth in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, alongside continued market growth. STELARA declined 5.4%, which reflects continued competitive pressures from biosimilars and the ongoing shift toward novel classes. Growth in other immunology is driven by IMDEE and ICOTYDE launch uptake in the U.S. In neuroscience, SPRAVATO grew 36%, driven by continued share gains reflecting strong physician adoption and increased patient demand. CAPLYTA showed significant growth of 66.1%, driven by strong, continued launch momentum in adjunctive major depressive disorder and continued demand increases across bipolar disorder and schizophrenia. Now moving to MedTech. Worldwide sales of $8.6 billion increased 2.5%, with growth of 4.8% in the U.S. and 0.1% outside the U.S. Overall, cardiovascular grew 4.1%, including 20 basis points related to acquisitions. Electrophysiology delivered growth of 4.4%, driven by procedure expansion, commercial execution, and new product performance, partially offset by competitive PFA pressures, which were more pronounced in Asia-Pacific this quarter, as well as the lapping of prior-year O-U.S. inventory dynamics. Abiomed saw a decline of 1.5% due to lower patient volume. There are encouraging signals in the U.S. performance, with improvement in the quarter, supported by acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, and Impella 5.5 continuing to gain adoption. Shockwave grew double

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: digits at 17.2%, driven by continued adoption of coronary and peripheral products as well as new product launches, and reimbursement in the office-based lab setting within the U.S. Surgery saw a decline of 1%, including a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points from divestitures. The decline was more notably driven by ongoing expansion of VBP in China, the surgery transformation program outcomes across the portfolio, and Middle East disruption, which impacted tender timing and ordering patterns. The decline was partially offset by portfolio strength, driven by recent innovations such as Echelon 400 and Duo, as well as commercial execution in biosurgery. Vision growth was 5.1%, driven by premium innovation, strong execution, and global reach. Contact lenses and other products grew 4.3%, driven by strong performance in the ACUVUE OASYS 1-Day family of products, further solidifying our leadership position, partially offset by U.S. inventory dynamics. Surgical vision delivered growth of 7.1%, driven by new product innovations, robust demand for premium IOLs, and strong commercial execution, partially offset by market-specific factors such as disruptions in the Middle East. Orthopedics growth for the quarter was 3.4%, primarily driven by new product launches such as VOLT in Trauma and EMPHASYS in Hips, including strong commercial execution in VELYS pull-through and knees. Now turning to our consolidated statement of earnings for the third quarter of 2026. I would like

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: to highlight a few noteworthy items that have changed compared to the same quarter of last year. Cost of goods sold deleveraged by 150 basis points, driven by unfavorable product sales mix and increased intangible asset amortization expense in the Innovative Medicine segment for intracellular, partially offset by the impact of tariff recoveries in the MedTech business. Selling, marketing, and administrative expenses were flat as a percent of sales, reflecting consistent commercial investments in the Innovative Medicine business. We continue to invest strategically in research and development, deploying approximately $4.7 billion, or 18.3% of sales, which includes $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly Bio. In-process research and development impairment of $339 million in the quarter is related to the write-off of PreCardia, a non-core asset acquired as part of the broader Abiomed transaction. Other income and expense was a net expense of $5.8 billion compared to $478 million of income in the third quarter of 2025, with the change primarily driven by the proposed talc litigation resolution and orthopedic separation-related costs. The tax rate was a small net benefit in the quarter, primarily related to the positive tax effect associated with the accrual for the proposed talc litigation resolution. More information can be found in our upcoming 10-Q regarding changes in taxes. Lastly, I will direct your attention to the box section of the slide, where we have also

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: provided our income before tax, net earnings, and earnings per share adjusted to exclude the impact of intangible amortization expense and special items. Now let's look at the adjusted income before tax by segment for the quarter. Innovative Medicine margin declined from 44.3% to 35.4%, primarily due to acquired in-process research and development expense of approximately $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly Bio, transaction costs for Cell BioMedicines, and unfavorable product sales mix and cost of products sold. MedTech margin increased from 21% to 22.9%, driven by the impact of tariff recoveries, partially offset by increased strategic investments in commercial capabilities. As a result, adjusted income before tax for the enterprise as a percentage of sales decreased from 35.2% to 30.2%. This concludes the sales and earnings portion of the call. I will now turn the call over to Joe.

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO: Thanks, Ryan. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. As you heard from Joaquin and Ryan, our third-quarter results were driven by the strength of our Innovative Medicine business. This performance more than offset headwinds in certain areas of MedTech, enabling us to exceed expectations on both the top and bottom line while continuing to invest in our pipeline and future growth. We are clear on where MedTech performance needs to improve, specifically cardiovascular and surgery outside the U.S., and are taking action to strengthen results. While disappointing, the underlying fundamentals of the MedTech business remain strong, supporting our confidence in the long term for that business. Across Johnson & Johnson, the drivers underpinning our outlook remain firmly in place. As a result, we are raising our guidance for 2026 versus our most recent update in July. The depth of our portfolio, momentum from new product launches, and upcoming pipeline catalysts further reinforce our conviction in achieving double-digit growth by the end of this decade, with sustainable growth beyond. Turning to financial metrics and our cash position, we ended the third quarter with approximately $17 billion of cash and marketable securities and approximately $45 billion of debt, for a net debt position of approximately $28 billion, generating more than $6 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter. We remain confident in our full-year free cash flow guidance of

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: $21 billion. During the quarter, we completed the $1 billion acquisition of Firefly Bio, deepening capabilities in oncology with next-generation antibody engineering to address complex tumor biology. As Joaquin referenced earlier, we also entered into a collaboration with Cell BioMedicines to advance in vivo CAR T therapies for immune-mediated diseases. Our disciplined approach to capital allocation is centered on prioritizing investments that support key commercial launches, accelerate future innovation, increase our annual dividend, and strengthen our pipeline through strategic, value-creating inorganic opportunities. In July, we announced an agreement for a resolution of the ovarian talc litigation for $5.5 billion, which is reflected in our third-quarter GAAP results. The agreement is conditioned upon the express participation of at least 95% of claimants and meeting a 95% threshold. Let me now turn to full-year 2026 guidance. As always, our outlook reflects what we know today regarding foreign exchange rates, the broader macroeconomic environment, and other external factors. Based on our year-to-date performance and expectations for the fourth quarter, we are raising the midpoint and tightening the range of our operational sales guidance. We now expect full-year operational sales growth in the range of 6.7% to 7.1%, which represents operational sales of $100.7 billion at the midpoint, or growth of 6.9%. We do not speculate on future currency movements. As of last week,

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: the euro spot rate to the U.S. dollar was 1.12. However, the average rate for the fiscal year stands at 1.15. Based on that average rate, we estimate reported sales growth of 7.2% to 7.6%, with a midpoint of $101.2 billion, or 7.4%. Assuming the current spot rate holds into next year, we could expect currency to be a headwind. Turning now to other items of the P&L. Regarding operating margin, we now expect a decline of approximately 60 basis points. This is an improvement from the 75-basis-point decline reflected in our updated July guidance, which included the impact of the Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines transactions, which had an unfavorable impact of 150 basis points. Absent those deals, we continue to deliver base margin improvement. As a reminder, our pretax adjusted operating margin outlook also reflects the cost associated with the 53rd week of operations and our previously announced agreement with the U.S. government to improve access to medicines. For net interest expense, we are lowering our guidance to $150 million to $200 million. We are also tightening the range of our effective tax rate guidance. Based on our year-to-date results, we now expect a full-year effective tax rate of 17.0% to 17.5%. Given those updates, we now expect adjusted operational earnings per share in the range of $10.95 to $11.05, or 2% at the midpoint. We expect reported adjusted earnings per share of $11.05 to $11.15, with a midpoint of $11.10, or growth of 2.9%. Excluding the impact

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: of Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines transactions of $0.64, reported EPS growth would approach 9%. As a reminder for your 2027 modeling, we expect Firefly Bio and Cell BioMedicines to have a combined dilutive impact of $1.36 per share on full-year adjusted earnings per share next year. We will provide more details on our 2027 outlook later this year at our Enterprise Business Review. Let me now highlight several upcoming developments that reinforce our growth outlook and performance for the remainder of the year. In oncology, we expect several important data readouts in the fourth quarter. These include data for pasaritomab, a first-in-class bispecific antibody in patients with advanced prostate cancer who have progressed after multiple lines of therapy. We also expect data for JNJ-6.11, an investigational first-in-class once-daily oral therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. We continue to see strong adoption for INLEXZO, with year-to-date sales of approximately $200 million, and expect to build on that momentum with a data readout in high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer later this year. We also expect U.S. approval of RYBREVANT FASPRO in advanced head and neck cancer. In immunology, as Joaquin referenced earlier, ICOTYDE is off to a strong start, and we look forward to presenting data in psoriatic arthritis later this year. In MedTech, we expect U.S. approval of VARIPULSE Pro in the fourth quarter, further complementing last week's approval in

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Japan. In heart recovery, we are taking corrective action to improve Abiomed's performance. We continue to invest in clinical evidence and expect results from the HR PCI PROTECT IV trial in 2027. The trial will have 1,250 patients, four times more than the SHOCK-III study. This large-scale study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of Abiomed's Impella CP pump during high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention. In surgery, we are focused on commercializing OTTAVA following its recent FDA de novo authorization. We expect adoption and revenue contribution to build over time, with the goal of establishing OTTAVA as a significant pillar of our surgery portfolio by the end of the decade. Regarding orthopedics, we remain on track for the planned separation of DePuy Synthes by mid-2027. I am really proud of the team working to evaluate all separation vehicles, and all options are better positioned today than when we announced our intentions with this business. Given the way DePuy Synthes is performing and the momentum Nimesh Nana and his team are generating, we are leaning toward a spin as being the best option to create long-term value for Johnson & Johnson shareholders. That has always been our base plan, and we are confident that it can be successfully executed. We will provide additional updates as appropriate and when there is more information to share. Finally, I am really looking forward to, and hope you join us for, the Enterprise Business Review on December 8. At that

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: event, we will provide additional perspective on our 2027 outlook and the key drivers that reinforce our conviction in achieving double-digit growth by the end of the decade. Perhaps more importantly, we will highlight our earlier-stage pipeline and how it represents the next wave of growth into the next decade. Attendees will also have the opportunity to experience firsthand some of our latest innovations, such as OTTAVA. 2026 is on track for another successful year, exceeding expectations set at the beginning of the year. We look forward to closing out 2026 strong and setting up 2027 for continued success. Thank you to our colleagues, whose dedication and commitment continue to advance innovation, improve patient outcomes, and create long-term value for shareholders. With that, we are ready to answer your questions. Kevin, can you please open the call for Q&A?

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Certainly. We will now be conducting a question-and-answer session. If you would like to withdraw your question, please press *, then 2. We ask that you please limit yourselves to one question only. The first question today is coming from Asad Haider from Goldman Sachs. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Asad Haider, Analyst
passages.text: Asad Haider, Analyst: Great. Thanks for taking the question, and congratulations on all the progress. I have one point of clarification. On the double-digit growth by the end of the decade, the vocabulary in the press release references the progress in the underlying business, quote, together with strategic investments. I just want to be clear that refers to internal investments and not M&A. That is a question we are getting this morning. And then, Joe, on your comments that you are not satisfied with the MedTech performance and are taking action to strengthen that growth, is the implication there that you now feel more urgency to add to high-growth areas via M&A in MedTech? Do you think that you have the product portfolio today to drive the improved performance you are looking for? Thank you.

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO: Yes, Asad. Thank you for your questions. On the first aspect, that is correct. Your view of that being internal strategic investments is what will propel us to double-digit growth by the end of this decade, with increasing performance in the coming years. So that is the correct interpretation. It does not assume any inorganic additions at this moment in time. We are always on the lookout for strategic drivers that could complement our business, that make sense to be in our hands versus where the asset would currently reside, but also create value for the risk we are bearing on behalf of shareholders. With respect to the urgency, it is an urgency to fix what we currently have. We like the portfolio and the construct that currently exists with the three focus areas of vision care, surgery, and cardiovascular. I think you are very familiar, and maybe I will even hand it over to Timothy to talk about some of the things we are doing in heart recovery specifically to address that. What I would say is now a stable business, but we want to catalyze it back to double-digit growth. We are very excited about what is on the horizon for surgery, with the addition of OTTAVA over time. That will be a significant contributor to growth by the end of the decade. And then, as I mentioned earlier, Vision seems to be functioning well, both on the surgery side and the contact lens side, where we are the market leader. But, Tim, maybe you want to offer a comment or two around

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Abiomed?

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech: Sure, Joe. So, Asad, ultimately, Abiomed remains a temporary headwind, as you saw in Q3, but our conviction in the long-term opportunity has not changed at all. The slowdown we are seeing continues to be the same issue we highlighted in the quarter before, which is the study outside of the U.S. focused on high-risk PCI. Importantly, we do not view these challenges as structural in nature or as ones that will drive a long-term impact on the business. We are not seeing any changes in patient need, reimbursement access, or meaningful competitive pressures. We have also highlighted some questions we have around the study, including whether best practices were used in the study. Our focus today is really on education and advancing the clinical evidence base to show the incredible impact Abiomed has in both saving and improving lives. We believe it is a short-term headwind. It is important to recognize that in any emerging area of science, there is always going to be debate and discussion. Our responsibility is to continue to advance the evidence base in the best interest of patients. In the case of Abiomed, we are doing exactly that. It is a short-term headwind, but we are very confident this is going to be a strong platform for growth for Johnson & Johnson in the future.

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO: Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question today is coming from Larry Biegelsen from Wells Fargo. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Larry Biegelsen, Analyst
passages.text: Larry Biegelsen, Analyst: Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. Joe, I wanted to ask about the 2027 comments you made at Deutsche Bank. On the top line, you said you expect reported sales growth to be similar to 2026 after adjusting 100 basis points for the extra week in both years, which I think would mean about 5.4% reported growth next year. And on EPS, how should we think about your ability to grow earnings excluding IPR&D? And just remind us how much the Firefly, Cell dilution is IPR&D this year and next year. Thank you.

passages.heading: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO
passages.text: Joseph J. Wolk, CFO: So, for this year, the IPR&D dilution is $0.64, and for next year, the combination of those deals is $1.36. The way I would think about that, Larry—and you have covered us long enough where you know that typically our income growth or EPS growth will be a little bit better than our sales growth—that is how you can think about that next year after adjusting for the $1.36 adjustment. We will continue to look at margin improvement as part of the orthopedic separation, looking more holistically at our business, and some of the advances we are getting with technology and getting us more efficient across all parts of our business. That is probably a good way to frame your thinking now for 2027, but we will be a little bit more explicit on December 8 at our Investor Day. We will outline specifically the components to that and probably provide a pro forma with respect to the orthopedic separation, should that occur at some point next year, as well as a longer-term outlook.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Thanks. The next question is coming from Christopher Schott from JPMorgan Chase. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Christopher Schott, Analyst
passages.text: Christopher Schott, Analyst: Great. Thanks so much. Just wanted to touch base on ICOTYDE. This is a two-part question. Can you give us an update in terms of what you are seeing regarding patient uptake as we think about new-to-biologic versus oral switches versus injectable switches? And then, bigger picture for the drug, are you talking about this as a $10 billion-plus asset? When you think about this very strong launch we have seen so far in psoriasis, with a number of additional indications pending, how do you think about whether this could be a much larger asset than $10 billion as you think about the peak sales opportunity for ICOTYDE? Thanks so much.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Great. Christopher, it is Tom. Good to hear from you. First, I do want to start by recognizing Jennifer Taubert and thanking her for her tremendous leadership and partnership. Jennifer leaves Innovative Medicine incredibly well positioned, as you see from our quarterly earnings, with strong momentum, an outstanding portfolio and pipeline, and, most importantly, a great team. We are fortunate to build on that foundation she established, and I am excited about what is ahead. Really, what I am excited about is what you are touching on right now: ICOTYDE. We do foresee ICOTYDE to be one of our biggest assets in Innovative Medicine, and it is off to an incredibly great start. As you highlighted, and as Joaquin highlighted on the call this morning, I think getting into some of the launch performance, you heard it from Joaquin already: to date, we have seen over 20,000 patients initiated on therapy, with over 8,000 prescribers—or nearly 9,000 prescribers, I would say. So, absolutely tracking better than most launches in psoriatic diseases. I think early prescribing trends are what you wanted to get at, as we think about the launch. We are expanding the systemic marketplace. Approximately 60% of the patients are systemic-naive, so they have not received any systemic therapy. Of the remaining 40%, roughly 20% are sourced from orals and 20% are sourced from other treatments, most likely biologics as we

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: dig into the data. So, as you are seeing with the launch performance, there is a bit of expansion of the marketplace. Absolutely, there is an opportunity to continue to drive that. As Joaquin highlighted earlier, I think it is important to point out that we do have broad commercial access now and preferred access in place on all national commercial plans, or are actively engaged to expand that to the Medicaid and Medicare population. I would say we are very excited about the launch to date and equally as excited about the future. We do foresee this to be one of our largest assets, as I pointed out. We are excited about the upcoming data readouts, both with the PsA Phase 3 data and the head-to-head STELARA data for ASCEND that we should be releasing in the coming months. As we look to expand beyond that, we will get into more of this at the EBR, including IBD and expansions into UC and CD, where we expect similar results with regard to launch performance. Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: The next question is coming from Joanne Wuensch from Citi. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Joanne Wuensch, Analyst
passages.text: Joanne Wuensch, Analyst: Good morning, and thank you for taking the question. I want to focus a little bit on MedTech here. When you use the phrase that the underlying fundamentals in MedTech are solid, I want to confirm that you are thinking about all the good stuff: patient volumes, capital expenditure spending from the hospitals, and what you are seeing in terms of general flows. And then, as a related question, what do you think needs to be done to improve the Johnson & Johnson franchise? Thank you.

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech: Joanne, it is Timothy. Thank you very much for the question. Let me start by really putting the overall MedTech Q3 results in context for you and everyone on the call. To be clear, our performance is below the standard we have set internally and below the expectations we previously communicated to investors. Simply put, we can do better, and we absolutely will. Right now, we are focused solely on the actions needed to deliver stronger results in the fourth quarter and beyond. That said, to your question, when we break down our results, you will see that the pressure was primarily concentrated in two very distinct areas. Firstly, our performance outside of the U.S. Secondly, Abiomed globally, which we have already touched on. To put it in perspective, growth in the U.S., which is the most important market, was in fact robust in the quarter and accelerated to almost 5%. Our performance outside of the U.S. was a challenge, and it reflected a combination of mostly known headwinds, which we have discussed previously. For example, in surgery, the expected impact of the transformation program and the ongoing expansion of volume-based procurement in China. In electrophysiology, competitive intensity, especially in Asia-Pacific, which is a region that is still relatively early in the adoption of PFA. We did introduce a new headwind, which is the incremental pressure that we are seeing on the business due to the

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: conflict in the Middle East. When you step back and look deeper into these results, we are seeing several encouraging indicators that give us confidence in a stronger Q4 and outlook beyond that. For example, in electrophysiology in markets like Europe, where we have already launched VARIPULSE Pro—which, by the way, is a faster and easier-to-use catheter—we are back to double-digit growth. We will launch VARIPULSE Pro in Japan shortly after receiving regulatory approval last week. You can also anticipate a U.S. launch by the end of this year. At Abiomed, we have already touched on the study in PCI, a study where we actually believe that the methodology employed did not follow well-established practices, an issue which we are addressing through education. We think we are going to get through that because the evidence base is so solid, especially in areas like AMI shock, and we are still seeing tremendous performance of 5.5. We did already see some improvement sequentially throughout the quarter, and we do believe that business will be back to growth in short order. While Q3 for MedTech was not a strong quarter, this should not distort the whole picture. As mentioned, the issues are primarily concentrated in the two areas I mentioned. It is also worth reinforcing, in response to your question, that the underlying procedure environment remains stable across key markets. I know there has been a lot of debate about that. Our job now is to make sure that we convert that demand

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: into more consistent performance. We remain confident in the combination of the momentum we are seeing in the U.S. and the moderation of these near-term headwinds, which will support improved performance in Q4 while positioning us for stronger performance in 2027 and beyond. As you have already heard from Joaquin and Joe, we will share more detail around what that looks like for 2027 and beyond, specifically with a focus on new innovations like OTTAVA, when we come together on December 8. Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: The next question today is coming from Jason Gerberry from Bank of America. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Richard Wagner, Analyst
passages.text: Richard Wagner, Analyst: Hello. This is Richard Wagner for Jason. I had a question regarding the ICOTYDE psoriasis launch. Are there lessons that can be learned that would be useful when ICOTYDE launches in IBD? Specifically, IBD competitors are developing high-efficacy combination programs, and I am wondering how that could affect physicians' perception of ICOTYDE's efficacy. Thank you.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Hi, Richard. It is Tom addressing your question. A couple of things I would point out, and I would obviously turn it over to John if he has any further remarks with regard to it. We absolutely know the space very well, whether it be in psoriasis or IBD. You could tell by the launch that we had with Tremfya in IBD that it is off to an incredibly great start. As you can see, over 70% growth year over year and heavily penetrated, becoming the fastest-growing biologic across all indications, particularly in IBD new patient starts. So we know this space very well. With that said, there is still significant unmet need in a large number of patients who are untreated or not treated earlier in the course of their diseases. We see that as a great opportunity for not only market expansion, as we are seeing in psoriatic disease or psoriasis with ICOTYDE, but also because the profile of the product fits beautifully in that spot. Obviously, the data will determine how we look at it and position it once it becomes available in the marketplace. I will tell you, we will have early access as one of the other keys, and we will see rapid uptake once we get the data results. John?

passages.heading: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development
passages.text: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development: Yeah. Maybe just to build on that a little bit: I think the reason that we have had such a great start in psoriasis is because of that trifecta of biologic-like efficacy coupled with placebo-like safety, combined with the convenience of a once-a-day pill. We think that will play very well across all indications, including IBD, where, as Tom referenced, a large percentage of patients are still not on an advanced therapy. The data in our Phase 2 study were quite encouraging and look like ICOTYDE can deliver on par with the current monotherapy. Of course, we are very aware that some patients need something more, that they need combination therapy. That is why we are developing JNJ-4.8, which pairs our guselkumab, our IL-23 inhibitor, with golimumab, our TNF inhibitor, and is now in Phase 3 studies after really compelling Phase 2 data. Those data showed that in that refractory population—which had failed two or more prior advanced therapies—this combination delivers superior efficacy to the monotherapy. We are actively pursuing that for those patients where a monotherapy is not enough. We could then see the opportunity to move patients, if needed, beyond the monotherapies to the dual therapies with our co-antibody therapeutic, JNJ-4.8. Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question is coming from Vamil Divan from Guggenheim Securities. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Vamil Divan, Analyst
passages.text: Vamil Divan, Analyst: Great. Thanks for taking the question. Maybe one follow-up and then one actual question. Following up on ICOTYDE, I appreciate the comments you have made so far. I am curious if you would be willing to provide any commentary around actual net sales in the quarter or how it compares to where consensus was. We are just getting some questions from investors on that specifically. My other question is around INLEXZO. I appreciate the comments you made there around sales so far. I am wondering if you could quantify how you see the market opportunity expanding based on the current indication, and then what sort of opportunity the SUNRISE-5 data represents relative to what you have currently. Thank you.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Yeah. Obviously, we have not disclosed any sales for ICOTYDE, but I am confident we are going to be doing that next year, just based on the momentum and progress that we are seeing with the launch of ICOTYDE. Turning over to INLEXZO, also another exciting product that we have, or even a platform as we think about TAR-210 as well, and the opportunity that exists for us. We are off to an incredibly great start. Joe disclosed that we are nearly $200 million in net trade sales year to date. Quite honestly, we have not reported quarterly sales, but I could say that Q3 was north of $90 million. So we are seeing great sequential growth. This quarter, we saw new patient starts grow 45% versus the previous quarter. I wanted to point out that this is in a population in high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ. It represents roughly 4,000 patients in totality, so it is relatively small in nature, and we are still seeing one in three patients being put on INLEXZO in this patient population. You touched on SUNRISE-5, which is a broader patient population of roughly 15,000 patients. What we call SUNRISE-3, which is the BCG-naive population, is roughly 50,000 patients. This is where we absolutely see a greater opportunity for us to live into the number of $5 billion-plus for the platform. I do believe we will do just that and above that, given the unmet medical need, the simplicity

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: that INLEXZO delivers, and the high response and durable complete remission rates that we are delivering with INLEXZO as we look to expand in the population. Maybe I will turn it to John to talk a little bit about the clinical development program.

passages.heading: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development
passages.text: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development: Indeed. As you know, the approval currently is for the cystitis-type non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, which spreads laterally. But the more common type is papillary. In our so-called SUNRISE-1 study, we had a cohort devoted to patients with papillary cancers, where those lesions that project outward from the bladder wall are excised by the urologist, and then INLEXZO is applied to try to prevent recurrence. We showed nearly 75% of patients had no recurrence after one year, and over 95% had no progression of their disease. In other words, they did not progress to more invasive types of disease. Based on that, the use of INLEXZO in that papillary form of the disease, which is by far the more common, is already in the NCCN guidelines. The FDA has invited us to submit for an expansion of our label into that population.

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO: Both ICOTYDE and INLEXZO, together with RYBREVANT, are going to be key drivers of our growth acceleration, driving us toward double-digit growth. They will become some of our largest products. Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question is coming from Michael Yee from UBS Securities. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Michael Yee, Analyst
passages.text: Michael Yee, Analyst: Great. Thank you for the questions. Maybe two pipeline science questions. On ICOTYDE, obviously you have great data in psoriasis, a little bit lower than biologics, but great data. In IBD, the UC data was quite strong. I am wondering if you think that would be replicated to biologic-like efficacy as an oral, and whether the differentiation there, due to the release in the gut, is a reason for the potentially stronger data in IBD, which could be a bigger driver. The second part of the question is on milvexian. I know you share in that partnership. Secondary stroke data are coming up, and I wanted to check in on your confidence that it should be similar to asundexian. That should be a fairly de-risked indication as a factor XI inhibitor. Thank you.

passages.heading: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development
passages.text: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development: John C. Reed here. Thanks for your questions. I will start off, and then maybe Tom will want to supplement. On ICOTYDE and IBD, we get that question all the time: might we see even greater efficacy with an oral because of the gut absorption? All I can say is, to be determined. We were quite pleased with the Phase 2 data in ulcerative colitis. I would also tell you that the Phase 3 studies, as we saw with our psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis studies, are enrolling briskly. The prior studies enrolled in about a third of the time that it normally takes us to enroll in those indications, reflecting, I think, the real enthusiasm that both physicians and patients have for this oral option. The theory about oral absorption and improved efficacy is to be determined by the data. Moving to milvexian, we remain confident in the studies underway, particularly with secondary stroke because of the asundexian data. As we know, in vitro, milvexian is a more potent inhibitor of factor XI. We have also been able to have a safety margin that allows us to push the dose to ranges that we are confident are quite effective. We remain confident in the results and expect that perhaps the secondary stroke data will be available even this year. It is an event-driven study. The atrial fibrillation study, in the larger population, will be next year. It will be exciting for us if we can prevail in both those

passages.heading: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development
passages.text: indications, because about 25% of patients who are candidates for secondary stroke have atrial fibrillation. That is probably why they had the stroke in the first place. If we can benefit both of those populations, that will be exciting. We are confident in the atrial fibrillation study as well. There, we were able to push the dose four times higher, given our safety margin in the drug. From monitoring the anticoagulation of the blood with laboratory tests, we feel we are in the right range to benefit patients and prevent thrombosis. Thank you for the question.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Yeah. I just want to reinforce what John has said. There is an absolute need for highly effective oral anticoagulation therapy with a reduced bleeding risk. In AFib alone, approximately 40% of patients eligible for oral anticoagulants are not receiving oral anticoagulants, typically due to concerns about potential safety and the bleeding risk associated with the current DOACs. Thank you.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question is coming from Jayson Bedford from Raymond James. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Jayson Bedford, Analyst
passages.text: Jayson Bedford, Analyst: Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. I just want to go back to the international MedTech business. Is there any way to quantify the impact of the dynamics in the Middle East and VBP? Timothy, I wanted to ask about international surgery. First, just to confirm, your view is that there has been no change to the underlying demand profile internationally. Second, I think Joe mentioned taking actions internationally for surgery. What are those actions? Thanks.

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech: Thank you, Jayson. Let me try to get to all of those. Let me start with the Middle East. Clearly, we have highlighted that as a new risk that has broadened over time. The effect is no longer limited to a few markets, as we initially thought. We have seen increased disruption to ordering patterns, tender timing, and spending decisions across a wider group of countries, unfortunately. We have also seen governments and health care systems become more cautious in their spending priorities, with some funding and procurement decisions taking longer than what we normally would expect. That has created a more meaningful impact on purchasing behavior than we saw earlier in the year. That said, I think it is important that we see this really as a short-term factor. The underlying issues have not changed. The clinical need remains intact, and we would expect many of these opportunities to be deferred rather than permanently lost. I think that is an important factor as it relates to any form of conflict, and certainly what we are seeing in the Middle East. On surgery, as I mentioned, we were actually really excited about the performance of the business in the U.S. Our issue really was outside of the U.S. and, as you know, was primarily driven by factors we have discussed before, such as the transformation program and volume-based procurement, and then the incremental pressure that we have just mentioned around the

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: Middle East. Despite those headwinds, we are focused on where we can have an impact, and we have a lot of opportunities. Wound closure growth continued to benefit. This is a category where we absolutely dominate, and that growth has been driven by innovation such as StrataFix and Plus Sutures. Biosurgery, another north-of-a-billion-dollar platform, delivered solid growth driven by key brands like FloSeal, Surgicel, and Vistaseal. We continue to see good traction with our endomechanical innovations such as ECHELON 3000 and Duo. We are confident that we will see continued growth in the U.S. and acceleration in EMEA and a return to growth overall in the fourth quarter. I do think it is also worth reinforcing our confidence in this business going forward. This was core to how we started Johnson & Johnson MedTech, and we are absolutely committed to it for the long term. I would say the biggest reason for confidence is the fact that we will be entering the surgical robotics space. Combined with our leadership positions across wound closure, biosurgery, and advanced instrumentation, we believe that OTTAVA gives us the opportunity to participate more fully in one of the most attractive and underpenetrated areas of surgery. As we continue to execute our portfolio transformation, advance innovation across the existing business, and prepare for the launch of OTTAVA, we remain confident in the long-term trajectory of the surgery franchise. We get a lot of questions on OTTAVA. Rest

passages.heading: Timothy Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech
passages.text: assured that when we come together for the meeting on December 8, we will provide perspective on the outlook for that innovation and further build your confidence in what we believe will be a material contributor to Johnson & Johnson's growth over the long term. Thank you, Jayson.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: We have time for one last question. Certainly. Our final question today is coming from Alexandria Hammond from Wolfe Research. Your line is now live.

passages.heading: Alexandria Hammond, Analyst
passages.text: Alexandria Hammond, Analyst: Thanks for squeezing me in. With the CARTITUDE V and VI trials advancing in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, how is Johnson & Johnson preparing to educate physicians and treatment centers for the potential shift to use earlier in the treatment journey? How should investors think about the potential to capture share from these existing frontline regimens? Thank you.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Hi, Alexandria. It is Tom. Thanks for the question. First and foremost, yes, we are anxiously awaiting for those trials to read out. I would say we are already doing that right now with CARTITUDE IV across the globe. CARVYKTI is available in over 20 markets, and we are seeing substantial share growth in the earlier-line settings. Roughly, in the U.S., 50% of the utilization of CARVYKTI lies in lines two and three. So there is becoming more familiarity with the product and access to the product, and excitement about it, predominantly due to the unmatched overall survival as early as line two of therapy that we see in the standard of care. We are already educating health care providers on the product and how they can use it earlier. Some of the education is centered around appropriate patient selection—the earlier, the better—as well as proper bridging and getting the patients to the highest level of MRD negativity to be effectively treated with CARVYKTI.

passages.heading: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development
passages.text: John C. Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development: Great. Maybe just to remind you, on top of that, at the recent myeloma meetings, we showed five-year follow-up data from the CARTITUDE study in the second line. It showed that about half of those patients enjoyed complete remission out to five years with no further treatment. So, one-and-done: five years of continued disease-free survival. Very exciting data.

passages.heading: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine
passages.text: Tom Cavanagh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine: Great. Thank you, John.

passages.heading: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations
passages.text: Ryan Koors, Vice President, Investor Relations: And thank you, Alexandria, for the question. Thanks to everyone for your questions and continued interest in our company. I will now turn the call over to Joaquin for some brief closing remarks.

passages.heading: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO
passages.text: Joaquin Duato, Chairman and CEO: Thank you for your questions and your engagement in today's call. As you can see, we continue to build momentum. Growth improved sequentially in the third quarter. We expect further acceleration in 2027, with a clear path to double-digit growth by the end of the decade. In Innovative Medicine, growth will come from both our existing portfolio, including DARZALEX and TREMFYA, and newer products such as ICOTYDE, RYBREVANT, and INLEXZO as they begin to contribute more meaningfully. We see similar opportunities in MedTech. The potential from our cardiovascular launches, including next-generation PFA and IVL catheters, additional data supporting Impella, and OTTAVA in robotic surgery are not yet fully reflected in our growth. Taken together, these drivers position Johnson & Johnson as one of the cleanest growth stories in health care. We will provide more details about our portfolio and later-stage pipeline at our Enterprise Business Review later in December. Thank you very much, and enjoy the rest of your day.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Thank you. This concludes today's Johnson & Johnson Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
